sources.title: Disney Plus, Hulu, and HBO Max are all over 50 percent off for Black Friday
US bill to speed up clean energy projects could also fast-track fossil fuels
GTA VI developers vote against unionization

en.title: Black Friday streaming discounts, GTA VI workers reject unionization, and clean energy bill advances
en.dek: Streaming services offer steep Black Friday discounts; GTA VI developers vote against unionization; US Senate passes bill speeding clean energy projects while also fast-tracking fossil fuels.
facts: Disney Plus, Hulu, and HBO Max are all over 50 percent off for Black Friday, with Disney Plus and Hulu bundle available for $4.99 per month with ads for a year.
Rockstar Games workers voted 75 percent against the Independent Workers Union of Great Britain recognition agreement, with only 25 percent of votes in favor of unionization.
The U.S. Senate passed the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act (BAAJA) on Nov. 19 with a 62-33 vote, aiming to speed up permitting for energy infrastructure projects.
Environmental organizations warn BAAJA will also fast-track fossil fuels by undermining environmental regulations such as the Clean Water Act and Endangered Species Act.
Proponents, including Senator Sheldon Whitehouse, say BAAJA lowers emissions by 1.5 gigatons through 2040; opponents, including Oceana and over 120 scientists, oppose the bill.
body: For Black Friday, major streaming services including Disney Plus, Hulu, and HBO Max are offering discounts of more than 50 percent off. The Disney Plus and Hulu bundle with ads is available for $4.99 per month for a year, saving subscribers $96 in total, while the ad-free bundle is on sale for $14.99 per month for 12 months. These deals are available through 11:59PM PT on November 30th.

Workers at Rockstar Games, the developer of Grand Theft Auto VI, voted 75 percent against a formal recognition agreement with the Independent Workers Union of Great Britain. The vote, which ran from November 12th through 26th covering the GTA VI launch, saw only 25 percent of votes in favor of unionization. The IWGB stated that workers will continue organizing informally despite the lack of formal recognition.

The U.S. Senate passed the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act (BAAJA) on Nov. 19 with a 62-33 vote, aiming to speed up permitting for energy infrastructure projects. The legislation would ease development for renewable energy and transmission lines, but environmental organizations warn it will also fast-track fossil fuels by undermining bedrock environmental laws including the Clean Water Act and Endangered Species Act.
en.context: The events occurred on Black Friday 2026, a major retail holiday, and follow a Senate vote on legislation affecting energy permitting and environmental review.
